title.narrative: Modernizing Uzbekistan National Innovation System Project

description.narrative: The PDO is to enable the development of a market-oriented National Innovation System in Uzbekistan.

The objective of the Modernizing Uzbekistan National Innovation System (MUNIS) Project for Uzbekistan is to enable the development of a market-oriented National Innovation System. The project has four components. (1) Improving research excellence and commercialization component will improve the capacity of public research to achieve international standards of research quality and enable the commercialization of research results. (2) Promoting innovation in the private sector component will increase private sector innovation in Uzbekistan. It comprises two subcomponents reflecting the dual needs of Uzbekistan at the current stage of development, namely enabling technology adoption by firms and diffusion and supporting the initial growth of R&D-driven innovation, as well as the expansion of a knowledge-based startup sector in Uzbekistan. (3) Supporting STI policy-making and reforms component will address the lack of adequate information about good policies and the weak capacity of policy-making organizations. Importantly, in addition to the support of enabling reforms for project activities, it will also support coordination and consensus building for the implementation of reforms aiming at the development and implementation of new Science Technology and Innovation Strategy of Uzbekistan. The component will finance (i) advisory work for the preparation of studies or draft regulations and policies; (ii) training (e.g., mini-courses) and study tours; and, (iii) consensus-building workshops. MID will encourage women's participation in these events. (4) Project management, and monitoring and evaluation component will support project implementation activities. It will finance the operational costs of the PMU and other related operational costs, including those incurred in the administration of the programs. The PMU will be responsible for the day-to-day implementation of project activities, and for fiduciary activities (including procurement, financial management, environmental and social compliance, reporting citizen engagement, project audits, and other functions).

title.narrative: Value of investment in research infrastructure

comment.narrative: Achieved. The reported value stands at USD 5,924,362.78, which is close to the planned target of USD 6 million. The PAD definition limits research infrastructure investments to the Public Research Institutes Modernization (PRIM), but needs to include significant allocations under the Research Excellence Program (REP). Both programs have financed procurement and installation of critical infrastructure, such as laboratory equipment, research facilities, and digital platforms, which collectively enhance the capacity of institutes to deliver high-quality research and innovation outcomes. The PMU has provided a consolidated list of infrastructure procured under both PRIM and REP, covering all relevant subprojects, which serves as a reliable source for cross-checking and verification. This demonstrates that investments have been well documented and tracked in line with project objectives.

title.narrative: Investment in research commercialization and innovation mobilized by the project

comment.narrative: The progress toward achievement of this indicator is monitored semi-annually by the PMU through technical reports submitted by beneficiaries and interviews with stakeholders under the RCP, BIRD, and ICP programs. Under the RCP, USD 1.2 million in grant funds have been committed to nine winning subprojects with mobilized co-financing of USD 0.2 million. Under the BIRD, 18 subprojects were awarded USD 9.4 million in grant financing with mobilized co-financing of USD 2.7 million. Under the ICP, 211 projects were awarded USD 9.6 million, matched by USD 13.9 million of co-financing. While the aggregated figure amounts to USD 16.8 million in mobilized investment, verification revealed that a number of projects were not able to fully complete their obligations. As a result, the actual mobilized amount is lower than initially reported.

title.narrative: Papers submitted for publication in peer-reviewed journals

comment.narrative: The indicator has been fully achieved and exceeded, with 131 submissions to date against the original target of 70. The complete list of submitted articles was carefully reviewed and verified, including both those already published in internationally peer-reviewed journals and those still under review. This verification ensures consistency with the PAD definition, which counts all submissions regardless of publication outcome. The strong performance reflects the impact of project-supported activities such as the English for Science program, which significantly enhanced the capacity of the researchers to prepare manuscripts for international outlets.

title.narrative: Investments in knowledge-based start-ups mobilized by the project

comment.narrative: Knowledge-based start-up is a company whose purpose is to bring technology products or services to market. These companies deliver new technology products or services or deliver existing technology products or services in new ways. The indicator depends on the implementation of the BIRD and RCP programs. Currently, 27 commercialization projects were selected for implementation under the RCP and BIRD with a total amount of 10.6 mln of grant financing and 3.9 mln mobilized private co-financing.

The indicator on the completion of institutional modernization plans (IMPs) under the Public Research Institutes Modernization (PRIM) program is progressing steadily, even though the formal completion of these plans is expected only in early 2026 due to the complexity and sequencing of activities involved. Currently, 24 PRIM subprojects are active, creating a critical mass for systemic reform across the public research sector. Within this portfolio, five “champion” institutes have been identified that are well positioned to deliver comprehensive modernization plans. These champions are expected to serve as examples and models for broader institutional transformation.

title.narrative: R&D projects implemented with support of the project

comment.narrative: On track. Total number of implemented R&D projects financed by the Research Excellence Program of the project. Under the two selection rounds of the REP, which provides grant financing to subprojects from eligible research institutes, 25 subprojects out of 199 applications were awarded, committing an entire $10 million of Loan proceeds allocated to this program. 1 subproject grant financing was terminated due to failure to comply with the program requirements. As of March 31, 2025 21 sub-projects have been completed.

title.narrative: Papers published in internationally peer-reviewed journals, based on research funded by the project

comment.narrative: The indicator has been fully achieved, with 57 publications in internationally peer-reviewed journals as of September 2025, surpassing the original target of 50. Data was collected by the PMU through semiannual technical reports from research teams and verified via journal database checks (Scopus, Web of Science) as well as cross-checking with acknowledgments to project support. The publications cover priority fields such as material sciences, renewable energy, biotechnology, ICT, and agricultural sciences, directly reflecting the project's objectives of strengthening research excellence and innovation capacity. Many of the journals are indexed in Scopus or Web of Science, including several in Q1 and Q2 quartiles, which highlights both the quality and international visibility of the outputs.

title.narrative: SMEs that introduced a new product/service

comment.narrative: Number of firms that introduced (a) products or services that are new to the market and (b) products or services that have significant improvements in capabilities, user friendliness, components or sub-systems. Significant improvements include new or significantly improved capabilities or other functions; technical specifications; components and materials; incorporated software; user friendliness. This does not include: i) minor changes; ii) regular seasonal changes; iii) routine upgrades, iv) purely aesthetic design changes that do not affect functionality; v) the resale of a good purchased from other enterprises. Gradual achievement of this indicator will start with the launch of BIRD and ICP programs.

comment.narrative: On track. Research commercialization includes the value of funds allocated for proof of concept, prototyping, initial batch of products for testing, and market patenting amongst others, including pure start-up funding. Currently, 9commercialization projects have been selected under RCP. Actual number of commercialization proposals implemented within the framework of MUNIS project will be determined after completing all selected RCP projects over 2024-2026.

title.narrative: Regulations disciplining the allocation of competitive funds for research and innovation reflecting the best practices adopted by MID

comment.narrative: The indicator has been fully achieved, as the MHESI has formally approved the manuals regulating the allocation of competitive research and innovation funds. These manuals provide the operational framework for all major MUNIS grant programs, including the REP, RCP, BIRD, ICP, and PRIM program. Each of these programs is governed by publicly available guidelines, which can be accessed on the official website of the project. The manuals ensure that funding decisions are based on meritocracy through independent expert review, that the process is transparent with clearly defined selection criteria and advance notice of calls, and that accountability is secured through detailed documentation of decision-making and publication of results.

title.narrative: Regulations for the management of research and innovation funding reflecting international best practices agreed between MID and NIS stakeholders

comment.narrative: Achieved, as regulations for the management of research and innovation funding that reflect international best practices were formally agreed between the Ministry of Innovative Development (MID, now the Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation) and key NIS stakeholders. The agreed framework incorporates the three core principles outlined in the PAD: meritocracy, ensured through the use of international peer review and the autonomy of decision-making bodies; transparency, guaranteed by clear selection criteria and advance notice of calls for proposals; and accountability, demonstrated by the documentation of responsibilities and public availability of key information. In the course of implementation, the PIU organized informational meetings to discuss and refine the grant program manuals, inviting representatives of research institutes, universities, private sector partners, and other NIS actors, ensuring validation.

comment.narrative: Achieved. The PAD indicator definition only accounts for R&D projects funded through the Research Excellence Program (REP). While 24 subprojects have already been implemented under REP, expanding the scope to include RCP (9 projects) and BIRD (18 projects), — which also contain significant R&D components—would provide a more comprehensive view of the project's contribution to research and development. Incorporating these programs increases the total to 51 projects, ensuring the indicator better reflects actual achievements and the broader impact of MUNIS in supporting innovation and commercialization. This adjustment is recommended to align the indicator with the project's evolving structure and objectives.

title.narrative: SMEs with internationally and nationally recognized certification funded by the project

comment.narrative: The progress toward achievement of this indicator was monitored by PMU on semi-annual basis through interviews with stakeholders, technical reports to be submitted by the consulting company that was hired to assist the program. The original target of 90 internationally recognized certifications was linked to the design of the Supplier Development Initiative (SDI), where one large corporate partner was expected to support SME projects in meeting global standards. However, with the transformation of the SDI into the Innovation Capacity Program (ICP), the implementation model shifted significantly. Under ICP, SMEs pursued certification independently, supported through program resources rather than through direct corporate facilitation. Given this change in design and implementation, the original focus on international certification alone has proven unrealistic within the project timeframe, as many SMEs require substantial time and resources to comply with global standards.

title.narrative: SMEs that introduced a new product/service

comment.narrative: Number of firms that introduced (a) products or services that are new to the market and (b) products or services that have significant improvements in capabilities, user friendliness, components or sub-systems. Significant improvements include new or significantly improved capabilities or other functions; technical specifications; components and materials; incorporated software; user friendliness. Moreover, MUNIS applies stringent verification standards to ensure that reported cases represent genuine innovation outcomes. Only SMEs that can demonstrate documented market launch, initial sales, or regulatory approvals are counted, which prioritizes credibility and sustainability of results over volume. This conservative approach inevitably lowers the raw number of SMEs but provides stronger assurance of impact and alignment with the PDO.

title.narrative: Research commercialization proposals implemented with support of the project

comment.narrative: Research commercialization includes the value of funds allocated for proof of concept, prototyping, initial batch of products for testing, and market patenting amongst others, including pure start-up funding. The PAD definition limits the scope to the Research Commercialization Program (RCP), which does not fully reflect the breadth of project-supported commercialization activities. It is therefore recommended to explicitly include the Business Investments in R&D (BIRD) program, which has provided significant financing for proof of concept, prototyping, product testing, and early commercialization activities. Both RCP and BIRD contribute directly to the project's objective of fostering innovation-driven commercialization, and their combined results offer a more accurate picture of progress.

title.narrative: Co-sponsor of the Supplier Development Initiative engaged by AID

comment.narrative: The indicator captures engagement of the co-sponsor of the Supplier Development Initiative (SDI) financed by the Innovation Capabilities Program (ICP, US$10 Million) of the project. The AID engaged the state-run Business Development Bank that finances small business projects and provides them with comprehensive services to support the program.

title.narrative: Satisfaction rate of grant applicants on the application process (reflecting transparency and meritocracy)

comment.narrative: The PMU dminister an online survey after each call for proposals for the grants programs, aimed at the targeted beneficiaries (including those who had successful applications, rejected applications, or who did not apply) to receive feedback on their perceptions of the meritocracy and transparency of the process. The feedback isreviewed by the grant administrating body to improve the subsequent calls for proposals. The PMU already has M&E specialist and the social specialist to follow the procedure. Collecting the feedback is tied to the first activity - the REP. The PIU has developed a questionnaire, reviewed by the Bank team,and launchedthe feedback collection among all the REP participants. The questions included, inter alia, the following: Was there discrimination (based on gender, nationality, education, etc) in the selection of the winners of the contest; and Are you satisfied with the objectivity of the work of the selection committee;According to the results of the feedback collection, there were 98respondents, which participated and were then rejected in the REP 1 andEP2 rounds. Survey results show current 100% satisfaction rate with the application process.Feedback will be collected following other grant programs implementation and results will be updated.

title.narrative: Satisfaction rate of grant applicants on the application process (reflecting transparency and meritocracy)

comment.narrative: The indicator is fully achieved, with survey results showing a high satisfaction rate among applicants (including those who had successful applications, rejected applications, or who did not apply) across all project programs. Evidence has been provided through completed questionnaires, which confirm positive perceptions of meritocracy, transparency, and fairness in the application process. To ensure alignment with observed performance and to reflect a more realistic benchmark, it is proposed to revise the target upward to 95%.

title.narrative: Grievance mechanism for all grants programs is established and implemented

comment.narrative: Achieved. A grievance redress mechanism will be established for each grant program to allow for appeals, complaints and feedback and ensure that the programs remain transparent, meritocratic and responsive to their targeted beneficiaries. The PIU is already equipped with staff to maintain the GRM. The launch of the mechanism came together with the launch of the first project activity, the REP. As of the ISR date no complaints or feedback from the REP or other project participants had been registered.
